function.name: requests_get
function.description: Send a GET request to a specified URL to retrieve all products and branches with triangulation runs in the latest 90 days. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: The URL to send the GET request to.

Content-Type.description: The MIME type of the body of the request (used with POST and PUT requests).

Accept.description: The MIME types that are acceptable for the response.

headers.description: Headers to include in the request as a dictionary of header names to header values.

timeout.description: The maximum time in seconds to wait for the server to send data before giving up. This is a float type value.

days.description: The number of days to look back for triangulation runs.

end_date.description: The end date for the data retrieval period, in the format 'YYYY-MM-DD'. If null, defaults to the current date.

params.description: Optional query parameters to include in the request.

auth.description: HTTP authentication credentials as a (username, password) tuple.

cert.description: Path to a certificate file to verify the peer.

cookies.description: Cookies to send with the request as a dictionary of cookie names to cookie values.

http.description: URL of the proxy for HTTP requests.

https.description: URL of the proxy for HTTPS requests.

proxies.description: Proxy settings as a dictionary mapping protocol names to URLs of the proxies.

stream.description: If true, the response should be streamed; otherwise, the response will be downloaded immediately.

verify.description: Whether to verify the server's TLS certificate or not.

message.content:
**Triangulation metrics** are quantitative indicators that describe how well a reconstructed triangular mesh (or surface) represents the underlying geometry it was meant to capture. They are used to compare two meshes—typically a *reconstructed* mesh against a *reference* (ground‑truth) mesh—or to evaluate the internal consistency of a single mesh (e.g., its smoothness or regularity). Below is an overview of the most common categories and specific metrics you’ll encounter: | Category | Typical Metric(s) | What It Measures | Why It Matters | |----------|------------------|-----------------|---------------| | **Accuracy / Fidelity** | • **Hausdorff Distance**
• **Chamfer Distance**
• **Root‑Mean‑Square (RMS) Error**
• **F‑score (precision + recall)** | How close the reconstructed surface is to the reference at each point. | Determines whether the reconstruction captures fine details or misses features. | | **Completeness / Coverage** | • **Recall (coverage)**
• **Precision (noise rejection)**
• **IoU (Intersection over Union)** | Proportion of the reference surface that has been captured vs. proportion of the reconstruction that matches the reference. | Indicates missing parts or extraneous artifacts. | | **Geometric Consistency** | • **Surface Area Difference**
• **Volume Difference**
• **Normal Vector Deviation** | Differences in global properties or local orientation between meshes. | Useful when absolute shape matters (e.g., engineering tolerances). | | **Mesh Quality** | • **Triangle Count / Edge Length Distribution**
• **Aspect Ratio**
• **Uniformity / Regularity** | Structural characteristics of the mesh itself. | Affects downstream processing such as simulation, rendering, or further refinement. | | **Noise & Smoothness** | • **Curvature Estimation Variance**
• **Edge Sharpness / Laplacian Smoothing Residual** | Degree of irregularities or jaggedness. | Helps decide if post‑processing (denoising, smoothing) is needed. | ### How These Metrics Are Calculated 1. **Point‑to‑Surface Distances** – For each vertex on one mesh, find the closest point on the other mesh and compute Euclidean distances. - *Hausdorff*: max of the two directed distances. - *Chamfer*: mean of the two directed distances. 2. **Area/Volume Integration** – Compute signed volumes or areas using divergence theorem or voxelization. 3. **Normals Comparison** – Dot product of corresponding normals gives angular deviation. 4. **Statistical Summaries** – Mean, median, standard deviation, percentiles (e.g., 95th percentile) give a fuller picture than a single scalar. ### Practical Use Cases | Scenario | Which Metrics Are Most Informative? | |----------|-------------------------------------| | Comparing two reconstructions from different sensors | Hausdorff, Chamfer, F‑score | | Evaluating a new reconstruction algorithm | All categories, especially Accuracy & Completeness | | Checking if a mesh meets CAD tolerance limits | Surface Area / Volume Difference, Normal Deviation | | Deciding whether to apply denoising | Curvature variance, Aspect ratio | | Assessing the effect of changing reconstruction parameters (e.g., point density) | Triangle count, Edge length distribution | ### Quick Reference Cheat Sheet | Metric | Formula (simplified) | Interpretation | |--------|----------------------|----------------| | **Hausdorff** | \( H(M_1,M_2)=\max(\sup_{p\in M_1}\inf_{q\in M_2}d(p,q), \sup_{q\in M_2}\inf_{p\in M_1}d(q,p)) \) | Worst‑case error | | **Chamfer** | \( C(M_1,M_2)=\frac{1}{|M_1|}\sum_{p\in M_1}\min_{q\in M_2}d^2(p,q)+\frac{1}{|M_2|}\sum_{q\in M_2}\min_{p\in M_1}d^2(q,p) \) | Average error | | **F‑score** | \( F=\frac{2PR}{P+R} \) where \( P=1-\text{error rate}, R=\text{recall} \) | Balance between precision & recall | | **Area Difference** | \( \Delta A = \frac{|A_{\text{ref}}-A_{\text{rec}}|}{A_{\text{ref}}} \) | Relative change in surface area | | **Volume Difference** | \( \Delta V = \frac{|V_{\text{ref}}-V_{\text{rec}}|}{V_{\text{ref}}} \) | Relative change in enclosed volume | --- #### Bottom Line Triangulation metrics provide a rigorous, objective way to judge the *quality* of a reconstructed mesh. By selecting the right combination of metrics for your application, you can pinpoint whether errors stem from missing geometry, noisy data, poor meshing choices, or algorithmic shortcomings—and then take targeted corrective action.
